name: Renew contracts and apply the general rate increase
summary: Each customer rate agreement comes up for renewal on its anniversary, and most are renewed in the autumn so new prices take effect with the January general rate increase. A pricing analyst reviews the account's profit and shipment history, sets a target increase, and either sends a standard increase letter or prepares a negotiation that the account executive leads with the customer, with approval from the pricing manager and, for large accounts, the vice-president of sales. Agreed pricing is drafted, signed, loaded into the rating engine and audited. The work bunches into a few weeks, customers take weeks to reply, and pricing loaded after the effective date causes rebills.

baseline.org_archetype: A Canadian LTL and truckload carrier of about 3,000 employees whose contract customers renew annually, with a ten-analyst pricing desk and 32 account executives.
baseline.notes: Covers renewals of customer-specific agreements; customers on the carrier's tariff with a discount receive the GRI without a renewal case. Rate agreements were kept as documents and spreadsheets, with prices keyed by hand into the rating engine, as was common in 2019-2022.

trigger: A customer rate agreement reaches its expiry or anniversary date, or the annual GRI is announced for agreements with a GRI clause.
end_state: Renewed pricing is loaded, audited and in effect, with any rebills issued, or the customer declines and the account goes to bid.

volume.seasonality: Most renewals fall in October to January ahead of January effective dates; mid-year anniversaries are spread over the rest of the year.

evidence.note: Volume from the organisation file (about 1,200 contract renewals a year among roughly 9,000 active accounts, most of which ship on tariff with a discount); author's estimate.

surge.cause: Annual general rate increase and contract renewal season

evidence.note: FreightWaves says GRIs are announced in Q3 or Q4 and implemented in Q1, which concentrates renewals; the multiplier is the organisation file's estimate.
About 16% of the ten analysts' time, concentrated in the autumn. Loaded cost from the organisation file (wage x 1.35 for salaried office staff).
About 6% of 32 account executives' time, more in the renewal season. Loaded cost from the organisation file (wage x 1.35 for salaried office staff).
Approvals of negotiated renewals. Loaded cost from the organisation file (wage x 1.35 for salaried office staff).
Approval of the largest renewals. Loaded cost from the organisation file (wage x 1.35 for salaried office staff).
First-invoice checks and rebills after pricing changes; not listed on this process in the organisation file. Loaded cost from the organisation file (wage x 1.35 for salaried office staff).

systems.name: Transportation management system (LTL and truckload operations, billing, rating)
Email, phone system and contact centre software

steps.name: Flag agreements coming up for renewal
steps.description: A monthly CRM report lists customer rate agreements that expire or reach their anniversary in the next 90 days, and agreements with a general rate increase clause that the January GRI will touch. The pricing manager assigns each to an analyst and account executive.

error.defect_description: An agreement with a wrong expiry date in the CRM is missed and rolls over at the old price.

evidence.note: ODFL says customers generally contract for one to two years, so every agreement comes up on a calendar; the monthly batch is the author's estimate.

steps.name: Pull the account's shipment and profit history
steps.description: The pricing analyst runs the account profitability report and pulls 12 months of shipments from the TMS: revenue, weight and density by lane, accessorials, claims, rebills and the operating ratio from the costing model. Accounts with a poor margin are marked for a larger increase.

error.defect_description: Profitability pulled on the wrong set of account numbers, missing some shipper locations.

evidence.note: Posting lists coordinating the annual GRI and updating rate agreements as pricing analyst work; queue of one to two weeks is the author's estimate, longer in the autumn renewal season.

steps.name: Analyse the account and set the target increase
steps.description: The analyst re-costs the account at current cost factors, compares its operating ratio with the target, and sets a target increase and a floor, usually starting from the published GRI of 5% to 7% and adding more for unprofitable lanes or density problems. The analyst writes a one-page recommendation.

error.defect_description: Increase set from outdated cost factors or without counting accessorial revenue.

evidence.note: FreightWaves gives 2021 GRIs of 4.9% to 7.9% and says carriers focus on overall account profitability; TForce took 6.9% in November 2021; times are the author's estimate.

steps.name: Decide standard increase or negotiation
steps.description: The analyst decides whether the account can take a standard increase by letter, which suits small and profitable accounts with an increase clause, or needs a negotiated renewal because it is large, unprofitable or likely to go to bid.

error.defect_description: None introduced; earlier errors pass through.

evidence.note: Split of 40% standard and 60% negotiated is the author's estimate.

steps.name: Account executive reviews the recommendation
steps.description: The account executive reads the recommendation and adds what the numbers do not show: competing bids the customer has mentioned, service failures, planned volume changes and the customer's budget timing. The executive and analyst agree the opening position and the walk-away floor.

error.defect_description: None introduced; earlier errors pass through.

evidence.note: Common LTL sales practice; times are the author's estimate.

steps.name: Pricing manager approves the renewal position
steps.description: The pricing manager checks the proposed increase and floor against the account's operating ratio and the network's lane balance, and approves, sends it back, or refers large accounts to the vice-president of sales. Counter-offers return here for a new floor.

error.defect_description: None introduced; earlier errors pass through.

control.basis: Pricing authority matrix: renewal floors set by the analyst approved by the pricing manager

evidence.note: Approval and referral shares are the author's estimates.

steps.name: Vice-president approves a large renewal
steps.description: The vice-president of sales reviews renewals for the largest accounts, where a loss would change terminal volumes, and confirms the floor and whether the carrier will walk away. The decision is often made in the weekly sales meeting.

error.defect_description: None introduced; earlier errors pass through.

control.basis: Pricing authority matrix: renewals above an annual revenue threshold approved by the vice-president of sales

evidence.note: Weekly meeting cadence is the author's estimate.

steps.name: Travel to the customer
steps.description: For larger accounts the account executive drives or flies to the customer's site for the renewal meeting, often combining it with other visits in the same city. The travel time is paid working time.

error.defect_description: None introduced; earlier errors pass through.

evidence.note: In-person meetings for about a third of negotiated renewals and travel of 30 minutes to six hours are the author's estimates; the wait is for a meeting slot in the customer's calendar.

steps.name: Present the renewal proposal
steps.description: The account executive presents the new pricing, explains the cost increases behind it (wages, equipment, fuel and insurance) and the service record, and listens for objections. The executive records the customer's response and any competitor prices in the CRM.

error.defect_description: None introduced; earlier errors pass through.

evidence.note: Common practice; times are the author's estimate.

steps.name: Await the customer's response
steps.description: The customer takes the proposal to its procurement or logistics manager, sometimes compares it with quotes from other carriers, and replies with acceptance, a counter-offer or a decision to put the business out to bid.

error.defect_description: None introduced; earlier errors pass through.

next.condition: customer goes to bid or leaves

evidence.note: ODFL notes customers solicit bids for one to two years of shipments; shares and response time are the author's estimates.

steps.name: Re-cost the counter-offer
steps.description: The analyst prices the customer's counter-offer or competitor price lane by lane, shows the margin at that level and suggests a compromise such as a smaller increase with a higher minimum charge or a density rule.

error.defect_description: Compromise priced without checking accessorial changes.

evidence.note: Common practice; times are the author's estimate.

steps.name: Record the agreed terms
steps.description: The account executive writes the agreed terms into the CRM opportunity and emails them to the analyst: discount, minimum charge, accessorial changes, fuel surcharge table, effective date and term. Terms agreed by phone are sometimes recorded incompletely.

error.defect_description: A term agreed verbally (an accessorial waiver or effective date) left out of the record.

evidence.note: Common practice; times are the author's estimate.

steps.name: Draft the renewal agreement
steps.description: The analyst prepares the renewal amendment or new rate agreement from the template with the agreed pricing, effective date and term, and sends it to the account executive for the customer's signature.

error.defect_description: Price or date typed differently from the agreed terms.

evidence.note: Common practice; times are the author's estimate.

steps.name: Send the standard increase letter
steps.description: For standard renewals the analyst merges the account's new prices into the increase notice template, states the effective date with at least 30 days' notice, and the account executive emails it to the customer.

error.defect_description: Notice sent to an outdated customer contact.

evidence.note: Carriers announce rate increases with an effective date ahead of time; notice period is the author's estimate.

steps.name: Await signature or acceptance
steps.description: The customer signs the agreement or, for standard increases, lets the notice period pass without objection. Some customers object to the standard increase and the renewal becomes a negotiation.

error.defect_description: None introduced; earlier errors pass through.

evidence.note: Shares and times are the author's estimates.

steps.name: Load the renewed pricing into the rating engine
steps.description: The analyst keys the new discount, minimums, accessorial exceptions and effective date into the rating engine for every account number covered. In the renewal season many agreements are loaded in the last weeks before the January effective date, and late loads mean shipments are rated at the old price.

error.defect_description: Wrong effective date or an account number left on the old pricing.

evidence.note: Posting describes updating rates and rate agreements in Truckmate; the late-load problem is described in the organisation file process entry; times are the author's estimate.

steps.name: Test-rate and audit the renewed pricing
steps.description: A second analyst rates sample shipments for each account number on the new pricing and compares them with the agreement. Errors go back for reloading.

error.defect_description: A loading error missed by the sample.

control.basis: Pricing department rule: a second analyst audits contract pricing before it takes effect

evidence.note: Common practice; error share is the author's estimate.

steps.name: Confirm the new pricing to customer, billing and service
steps.description: The analyst emails the account executive, billing and customer service the effective date and agreement number and updates the expiry date in the CRM so the next renewal is flagged. The account executive confirms to the customer.

error.defect_description: None introduced; earlier errors pass through.

evidence.note: Common practice; times are the author's estimate.

steps.name: Check the first invoices on the new pricing
steps.description: A billing auditor reviews the customer's first week of invoices after the effective date and compares the rated charges with the agreement. Shipments rated before the pricing was loaded, or on the wrong account, are flagged for rebilling.

error.defect_description: None introduced; earlier errors pass through.

control.basis: Billing quality control: first-invoice check after a pricing change

next.condition: shipments rated at old or wrong price

evidence.note: Rebill share of 10% is the author's estimate; billing-auditor is not listed on this process in the organisation file.

steps.name: Rebill shipments rated at the old price
steps.description: The billing auditor pulls every shipment rated since the effective date at the old or wrong price, re-rates it, issues corrected invoices and a cover note, and sends a pricing error report to the pricing manager.

error.defect_description: Some shipments missed in the rebill.

evidence.note: Times are the author's estimate; rebilling belongs to billing corrections but is shown here because late renewals cause it.

exceptions.name: Counter-offer
exceptions.description: The customer counters with a smaller increase or a competitor's price; the analyst re-costs it and it goes back through approval.

exceptions.name: Customer objects to a standard increase
exceptions.description: A customer who received the standard letter objects and the renewal becomes a negotiation.

exceptions.name: Late load causes rebills
exceptions.description: Pricing loaded after the effective date or on the wrong account is found in the first invoices and shipments are rebilled.

exceptions.name: Account goes to bid
exceptions.description: The customer rejects the renewal and runs an RFP, which the carrier answers through the RFP process.

benchmarks.unit: calendar days from the renewal flag to pricing in effect or the account lost

evidence.note: Author's estimate: renewals are flagged about 90 days ahead and most complete in four to eight weeks; no published figure was found.

benchmarks.unit: percent average increase on tariff base rates
benchmarks.population: North American LTL carriers, GRIs effective 2021 and early 2022

evidence.note: Stated in the sources: Old Dominion 4.9%, FedEx Freight and Estes 5.9%, ArcBest and TForce 6.9%, Forward Air 7.9%.

pain_points.description: Renewals bunch into the weeks before January, so analysts load pricing late and shipments are rated at the old price until rebills catch them.

evidence.note: The organisation file names late updates and rebills as the main problem; frequency is the author's estimate.

pain_points.description: Customers take weeks to respond and counter-offers repeat the analysis and approval loop.

evidence.note: Author's estimate of common practice.

pain_points.description: Terms agreed by phone are re-keyed from the CRM into an agreement and again into the rating engine, so details get lost.

evidence.note: Posting describes analysts updating rate agreements and rates in Truckmate by hand.

sources.title: Old Dominion Freight Line, Inc. Form 10-K for the year ended December 31, 2021
sources.supports: Many customers ship under the carrier's tariffs; customers generally solicit bids for relatively large numbers of shipments for one to two years; carriers compete on on-time performance and minimising cargo claims.

sources.title: Logistics Pricing Analyst (Calgary) job posting
sources.publisher: Lineage Logistics (via SJF Ventures job board)
sources.supports: Pricing analyst prepares spot quotes and cost checks, breaks down bids, costs opportunities in TCG costing software, maintains rate sheets, accessorials and fuel surcharge programs in Truckmate, works within the pricing department's approved guidelines and coordinates the annual general rate increase and rate agreement updates.

sources.title: LTL: How do general rate increases work?
sources.supports: GRIs raise base tariff rates while shippers keep negotiated discounts; GRIs are usually announced in Q3 or Q4 and take effect in Q1; only about 25% of ArcBest's and 20% to 25% of Saia's business is subject to the GRI, the rest is under contract or individual pricing; most carriers took a 5% to 6% GRI in Q1 2021 and many a second later in 2021.

sources.title: TForce Freight Announces Rate Changes (effective November 15, 2021)
sources.supports: Average 6.9% increase on non-contractual LTL shipments rated on tariffs including the 525 US/Canada tariff; does not apply to contractual shipments; accessorial charges also rise.

assumptions: The organisation file says renewals are triggered by the shipper's rate agreement; in practice the carrier starts the case from its own expiry calendar, which is modelled as a system step. The interface keeps the organisation file's trigger.
40% of renewals are standard increases by letter and 60% are negotiated; 12% of negotiated renewals end with the customer going to bid.
The renewal flag is generated about 90 days ahead, but the simulated cycle time starts when the flag is produced and includes up to four weeks before an analyst picks it up.

Billing auditors and the vice-president of sales take part although the organisation file lists only account executives, pricing analysts, the pricing manager and the vice-president on this process; the auditor is in the organisation file under finance.
The account profitability report is shown as an input from month-end close, as in the organisation file, but at most carriers the pricing or network analysts produce it from the costing model.
No step ties up vehicles, equipment or crews, so no resources are listed; no step is done by several people of one role together.
